item.title: Your Mouse Didn't Move, but the Menu Thinks It Did
item.description:
Picture a long menu with a scrollbar. A user opens it from the keyboard and walks down the items with the arrow keys, while their mouse just lies on the desk with the pointer somewhere over the panel. The list scrolls, a submenu trigger slides under the resting pointer, and its submenu pops open. One more arrow press, the trigger slides away, and the submenu closes again.

Nobody touched the mouse. The browser decided that the pointer had entered a new element, and the menu believed it. This guide shows why that happens, how to tell a hover the user made from one the browser made up, and how to test it.

item.title: How to create a dropdown menu in React
item.description: Creating accessible dropdown menus is essential for navigation and user interactions in React applications, requiring proper state management and keyboard support. As the creator of CoreUI, I’ve built countless dropdown components for enterprise applications. The most effective approach is using state to control visibility with click outside detection and keyboard event handling. This ensures accessible, user-friendly dropdown menus that work across all devices and input methods.
